s: A working bike shop and coffee counter on SE Powell Boulevard, staffed in part by at-risk teens learning barista and mechanic trades.
w: Braking Cycles runs a bike shop and espresso bar behind the same counter on SE Powell Boulevard, using both halves of the business to train at-risk youth through a partnership with the nonprofit Transitional Youth. The shop sells refurbished bikes ranging from kids' models to commuters and handles repairs, while the café pours Cascadia Coffee Roasters coffee and Jasmine Pearl tea alongside pastries from Hopes Bakery.
_facts: 3354 SE Powell Blvd, Portland, OR 97202
Nonprofit combining a bike shop and coffee bar; trains at-risk youth as baristas and mechanics via partner org Transitional Youth
Coffee from Cascadia Coffee Roasters, tea from Jasmine Pearl, pastries from Hopes Bakery

s: A bike shop and beer garden at the dead end of a Frogtown street, where the pavement meets the LA River bike path.
w: Spoke opened in 2015 as one of the first bike-shop-and-café hybrids in Los Angeles, sitting where N. Coolidge Avenue dead-ends into the Los Angeles River bike path in Elysian Valley. It has since grown from a coffee counter into a full kitchen and beer garden serving breakfast and lunch, while still renting and repairing bikes for riders on the river path.
_facts: 3050 N Coolidge Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90039
Opened 2015 as a bike shop/café combination, one of the first of its kind in LA
Expanded into a full-service restaurant and beer garden by 2017

s: A restaurant, bar, and boutique bike shop sharing one roof on Calabasas Road, at the foot of the Santa Monica Mountains climbs.
w: Pedalers Fork puts a scratch-kitchen restaurant, a full bar, a '10 Speed' coffee counter, and a working bike shop under one roof in Old Town Calabasas, a jumping-off point for road cyclists heading into the Santa Monica Mountains. The bike shop handles rentals, fittings and repairs, and the business runs organized 'Ride and Pint' group rides that start and end at the restaurant.
_facts: 23504 Calabasas Rd, Calabasas, CA 91302
Combines a restaurant/bar, a bike shop, and a coffee counter branded '10 Speed'
Hosts organized group rides ('Ride and Pint') departing from the location

a: Lady Bird Lake / Pfluger Bridge, Austin
s: The coffee bar built into Lance Armstrong's bike shop, moved in 2023 to the foot of a pedestrian bridge over Lady Bird Lake.
w: Juan Pelota Cafe operates inside Mellow Johnny's, the bike shop Lance Armstrong co-founded in 2008; the café's name riffs on his old cycling-days nickname. The shop and café relocated in 2023 from their longtime Nueces Street storefront to a new space at the foot of the James D. Pfluger pedestrian bridge, alongside the Lance Armstrong Bikeway and the Butler Hike-and-Bike Trail.
_facts: 115 Sandra Muraida Way, Suite 102, Austin, TX 78703
Mellow Johnny's Bike Shop founded 2008 by Lance Armstrong; Juan Pelota is its in-house café
Moved 2023 from 400 Nueces St to the current location at the foot of the Pfluger Bridge

a: Inner Richmond / Lone Mountain, San Francisco
s: A Richmond District breakfast counter whose whole menu is named for European climbs and the riders who suffered up them.
w: Velo Rouge takes its name and menu from owner Meg Lynch's cycling trips abroad; dishes are named for climbs like Mont Ventoux and racers like Coppi, Merckx, Indurain and Pantani. It sits on Arguello Boulevard a short ride from Golden Gate Park, with a patio and a recurring Radio Africa Kitchen pop-up on weekday evenings.
_facts: 798 Arguello Blvd, San Francisco, CA 94118
Menu items named after cycling climbs and champions
Near the Golden Gate Park entrance in the Inner Richmond/Lone Mountain area

s: A workbench and an espresso machine share the same room in Malasaña, and neither apologizes for the other.
w: Opened in Malasaña around 2013, La Bicicleta pairs a repair bench and tool wall with a coffee counter and a small coworking area; regulars borrow a pump or true a wheel between orders. Shelves hold cycling books and the calendar carries occasional talks tied to urban cycling.
_facts: Plaza de San Ildefonso 9, 28004 Madrid (Malasaña)
Combines café, bike workshop/tool bench, and coworking space
Operating since roughly 2013

s: In a century-old carpenter's workshop east of the Onyar, a former pro cyclist still pulls the shots.
w: La Fábrica occupies a converted early-20th-century carpentry workshop in Girona's old town, opened by retired professional cyclist Christian Meier and Amber Meier. It became a fixture for the city's resident pro-cycling colony and later spawned a sister roastery, Espresso Mafia.
_facts: Carrer de la Llebre 3, 17004 Girona (Barri Vell)
Founded by ex-professional cyclist Christian Meier and Amber Meier
Tied to sister roastery Espresso Mafia

s: A cycling outfitter's hub in Girona's old town where the espresso machine sits a few metres from the bike-fit stand.
w: Eat Sleep Cycle built its name renting road bikes to the pros' training crowd that colonised Girona; its Hub on Carrer dels Vern folds that workshop into a café serving specialty coffee, craft beer and brunch on a sun-facing terrace until 7pm daily.
_facts: Carrer dels Vern 3, 17004 Girona
Combines bike hire, workshop, apparel and café under one roof
Open daily 09:00-19:00

s: A showroom of steel and carbon frames in Kreuzberg, with a coffee pot going in back for whoever stops to look.
w: Standert's Berlin Cycling Hub functions primarily as a showroom and workshop for the frame brand, and is the meeting point for its regular group rides. Coffee is offered to visitors browsing bikes or booking a fitting rather than served from a standalone café counter.
_facts: Besselstraße 13, 10969 Berlin (Kreuzberg)
Meeting point for Standert's regular group rides

s: Espresso and gear cables under one roof in Wiehre, where the bicycle theme runs no deeper than the name and stays sincere for it.
w: Caffé Bicicletta has run on Brombergstraße in Freiburg's Wiehre district since June 2013, pairing a café counter with a small bicycle-themed retail corner. It draws a mix of neighbourhood regulars and cyclists passing through the district's quiet residential streets.
_facts: Brombergstraße 17, 79102 Freiburg im Breisgau (Wiehre)
Operating at this address since June 2013
Combines café with small bicycle retail shop

s: Illy espresso and Italian ice cream beside racks of vintage frames on the bank of the Isar, in a room Jan Ullrich once opened.
w: Monaco Velo Club runs its café inside the bikedress cycling store near the Isar in Au-Haidhausen, serving Illy coffee and Italian snacks, with gelato added in summer. Its opening event was fronted by former Tour de France winner Jan Ullrich.
_facts: Ohlmüllerstraße 7, 81541 München (Au-Haidhausen)
Café operates inside the bikedress cycling store
Opening event featured Jan Ullrich

s: Brunch plates and stripped steel frames share one storefront on Wilhelmstraße, between Potsdamer Platz and the Brandenburg Gate.
w: Steel Vintage Bikes Café combines an all-day breakfast and brunch menu with a retail floor of restored vintage road bikes, parts, and cycling clothing, in a Mitte storefront within walking distance of both Potsdamer Platz and the Brandenburg Gate.
_facts: Wilhelmstraße 91, 10117 Berlin (Mitte)
Combines café/brunch restaurant with vintage bicycle retail
Part of Steel Vintage Bikes, founded 2012

s: Cake and quiche between Warschauer Straße and Boxhagener Platz, in a bike shop that only really opens its doors a few days a week.
w: The Gentle Jaunt is a Friedrichshain bike shop for touring, gravel, and commuting builds that runs a small café serving cake, quiche, and Brazilian fair-trade coffee alongside its workshop. It keeps a limited schedule — Open Door Days on Tuesdays, Fridays, and every second Saturday.
_facts: Simon-Dach-Straße 20, 10245 Berlin (Friedrichshain)
Café serves cake, quiche, and Brazilian fair-trade coffee
Open Door Days: Tue, Fri, every 2nd Saturday; otherwise by appointment

s: A frame-building workshop by the Spree where the owner pours coffee while you look over the bikes.
w: 8bar's Mitte showroom, just north of Jannowitzbrücke, sells its custom-built frames and cycling gear alongside a small coffee-and-cake counter where visitors sit with the founder and staff. It is a shop first and a café second, but the coffee service is a fixed, advertised part of the space.
_facts: Köpenicker Straße 100, 10179 Berlin (Mitte)
Registered business explicitly includes sale of coffee, cakes and baked goods alongside bicycles
Hours: roughly Tue-Fri 12:00-18:00, Sat 12:00-16:00

s: Málaga's original bike-café, its dining room hung with frames and wheels, relocated in early 2026 to a new spot in the historic centre.
w: Recyclo opened as the city's first bicycle café, pairing a working repair shop with a kitchen turning out brunch, burgers and vegan plates under a ceiling of hanging bicycles. It moved from its longtime Plaza Enrique García-Herrera address to Calle Marqués de Villafiel in 2026, keeping the same bike-shop-doubling-as-diner format.
_facts: Calle Marqués de Villafiel 4, 29005 Málaga
Moved from Pl. Enrique García-Herrera 16 in 2026
Functions simultaneously as a working bike shop and full-service café/restaurant

s: The cycling apparel house's flagship by Nice's old port, where the brand's origin story as an actual café is still functioning, not just marketing copy.
w: Café du Cycliste takes its name literally at this Port Lympia address: alongside the full clothing collection and bikes for hire, the shop serves fresh-ground coffee at a counter styled after the traditional French café where the brand began in the hills above Nice.
_facts: 16 Quai des Docks, 06300 Nice
Combines coffee service, bike rental and the brand's clothing collection

s: Bordeaux's first bicycle café, run by two Anglophone transplants who deliver their own beans by bike from a local roaster.
w: Opened in 2017 by American Robert Lawrence and Briton Christopher Cooley, Musette pairs a gravel- and bikepacking-focused workshop with a coffee bar sourcing beans collected by bicycle from an independent Bordeaux roaster. A short Mediterranean-inspired lunch menu runs until 2pm.
_facts: 72 Cours de la Somme, 33800 Bordeaux (Nansouty)
First bicycle café in Bordeaux, opened 2017
Sources beans by bicycle from an independent local roaster

s: A café-restaurant, bike shop and workshop sitting at kilometre zero of the Bédoin ascent of Mont Ventoux.
w: Pista sits directly on the Route du Ventoux where the Bédoin climb begins, giving it a captive audience of riders fuelling up or recovering from the mountain. It runs specialty coffee, homemade lunches and local produce alongside a mechanical workshop and e-bike charging points.
_facts: 79 Chemin de la Ferraille, 84410 Bédoin
Located at Km 0 of the Bédoin ascent of Mont Ventoux
Open Wed-Sun 09:00-18:15, seasonally March-November

s: Paris's first dedicated cycling café, opened in 2015 in the 11th arrondissement, pouring coffee roasted a few streets away in Belleville.
w: Steel opened in May 2015 as Paris's first café built around cycling culture, and still runs as a hybrid: high-end cycling clothing and accessories on one side, espresso and filter coffee from La Brûlerie de Belleville with homemade pastries, quiches and sandwiches on the other.
_facts: 58 rue de la Fontaine au Roi, 75011 Paris
Opened May 2015, billed as the first cycling café in Paris
Coffee roasted locally by La Brûlerie de Belleville

s: Lake Como's original cycling café, where Lycra crowds a Borgo Vico coffee bar between climbs of the Ghisallo and the Muro di Sormano.
w: Sartoria Ciclistica grew from a made-in-Como cycling-apparel workshop into the town's clubhouse for riders, its espresso bar on Via Borgo Vico pouring a house blend named for three defining local climbs — the Ghisallo, the Muro di Sormano and the Val Fresca. During Giro di Lombardia week the shopfront turns into a stage for rider meet-and-greets and evening group rides.
_facts: Via Borgo Vico 54, Como
House coffee blend named after three Giro di Lombardia climbs
Hosts group rides and events during Giro di Lombardia week

s: A café, workshop and bike-rental hub at the foot of Monte Grappa, where the day's ride starts and ends over a proper V60.
w: Opened in 2024 by the Basso family — of Basso Bikes — Bassano Club House gathers a café, repair workshop, rental fleet and small hotel under one roof at the foot of Monte Grappa. The coffee side keeps it plain: filter, V60, espresso, alongside breakfast built for people about to ride or just off the bike.
_facts: Via Angarano 36, Bassano del Grappa
Founded 2024 by the Basso family (Basso Bikes)
Combines café, bike workshop, rental fleet and small hotel

s: The Kostner family's taverna at the foot of Col Alt, where a day among the Alta Badia climbs ends over a beer a short walk from the hotel's bike room.
w: Hotel Posta Zirm has stood on the slopes of Col Alt since 1908, still run by the Kostner family, and its attached Taverna is where the day's ride reliably ends. The hotel is built around cyclists, with a full bike room downstairs for washing and storing kit.
_facts: Strada Col Alt 95, Corvara
Hotel Posta Zirm run by the Kostner family since 1908
Dedicated bike storage/cleaning room used by touring cyclist groups

s: A cycling-apparel shop and specialty coffee bar in central Maastricht, founded by an ex-pro who traded the peloton for a portafilter.
w: Founder Brian Megens raced as a professional before opening Fixed Gear Coffee — first at Cauberg in Valkenburg in 2018, then a second shop on Grote Gracht in the heart of Maastricht in 2020. Cycling jerseys and boutique kit share shelf space with third-wave beans from roasters like Sey and White Label.
_facts: Grote Gracht 42, Maastricht
Founded by ex-professional cyclist Brian Megens and Shivani Achrekar
Second shop opened 2020, after a first location at Cauberg, Valkenburg (2018)

q: Lola Bikes and Coffee The Hague
s: A bike-and-coffee shop on The Hague's grandest street, near the royal palace, where espresso is served alongside vintage-look city bikes.
w: Lola Bikes & Coffee sits on Noordeinde, the same stately street as the Dutch king's working palace, pairing a small coffee bar with a shop that sells and repairs city and vintage-style bicycles. It's a fixture for bike commuters as much as for visitors drawn in by the palace-adjacent address.
_facts: Noordeinde 91, The Hague
Functions as both a working bike shop/repair point and a coffee bar
Located opposite the Noordeinde Palace shopping district

s: A proper fietscafé at the foot of the Amerongseberg, with showers, bike storage and a tourist office rolled into one converted building.
w: De Proloog — Dutch for 'the prologue' — occupies a former sheltered-housing building in Amerongen and runs it as a full cycling clubhouse: showers and changing rooms, secure bike storage, a workshop corner, and a café serving coffee, cake, soup and a proper lunch menu, plus the local VVV tourist-information desk.
_facts: Allemanswaard 27, Amerongen
Combines café, showers/changing rooms, secure bike storage and workshop space with a VVV tourist-info desk
Sits at the foot of the Amerongseberg climb on the Utrechtse Heuvelrug

s: A stylish cycle café halfway up Monchique's switchbacks, run by two cyclists who turned bike repair and speciality coffee into the town's unofficial rider's clubhouse.
w: Founded by Lee Eaton and Neil Wilson, Velochique sits in the historic centre of Monchique — the climb that anchors the Algarve's inland cycling scene — combining a bike shop and repair stand with a café serving speciality coffee, ceremonial matcha and a breakfast-through-lunch menu.
_facts: Rua Serpa Pinto 8, Monchique
Founded by Lee Eaton and Neil Wilson
Combines bike repair/shop with café
